alice: heads-up — hitting a latency floor on TP all-reduce for 8xA100 runs. At steady-state, all-reduce takes ~1.1ms for 256KB chunks and doesn't drop when we decrease chunk_count. NCCL v2.14.3 on cudnn 9.3. Kernel selection looks fine on the compute side, but comm isn't overlapping as expected. attaching quick trace.
ben: can you paste the timeline? is this across pipeline stages or tensor shards? also which backend (ring/tree/hierarchical) is being selected by NCCL?
alice: timeline pasted below. it's during residual add between TP shards (before KV cache refill). TP dims (tp=8) + pp=1. chunking enabled at the runtime (batching heuristic: prefer 128KB chunks). NCCL picks ring by default (env unset). trace excerpt:
```
[trace] t=0.000ms compute GEMM shard0 0.45ms
[trace] t=0.450ms enqueue allreduce chunk#3 0.02ms
[trace] t=0.470ms stall waiting for allreduce done 0.7ms
[trace] t=1.170ms resume compute GEMM shard1
```
carla: interesting — large gaps between enqueue and completion. suggests insufficient comm/compute overlap. did nvprof show any PCIe bursts or unexpected host-syncs? also curious if fusion thresholds are merging messages and creating a mid-size message sweet spot.
alice: nvprof snapshot shows steady small launches, no kernel syncs. but nccl op times spiking. run config: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`, `NCCL_ALGO=DEFAULT`, `NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=4` (default). we haven't tried NCCL_ALGO=RING or TREE explicitly.
devon: we should try explicit hierarchical (tree) and ring variants and measure latency vs message size. also try forcing `NCCL_BUFFSIZE` to split messages differently. quick test matrix:
- msgsize sweep: 64KB, 128KB, 256KB, 512KB
- NCCL_ALGO: RING, TREE (if supported), COLL
- chunk_count: 1, 2, 4
- enable/disable runtime chunk coalescing
carla: +1. i suspect runtime batching heuristics coalesce small token KV writes into mid-size segments, which hit a poor path in NCCL (inefficient chunk packing). Also check NIC saturation and channel concurrency.
perf-bot: profiling job 1825123456-1 completed -> s3://redwood-perf/1825123456/pprof.tar.gz :thumbsup:
ben: if you can, run a microbench: nvprof `nccl-tests` allreduce with the same message sizes and node config. that isolates runtime effects. also capture `nvidia-smi dmon` during run to see NIC/PCIe.
alice: ran nccl-tests allreduce microbench on same cluster. results (single iter median):
- 64KB -> 0.35ms
- 128KB -> 0.52ms
- 256KB -> 1.12ms  <-- weird jump
- 512KB -> 1.45ms
so 256KB is disproportionately bad.
carla: that strongly smells like fragmentation/algorithm change at that boundary. some NCCL implementations switch rendezvous/fusion strategies at specific thresholds. can you dump `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` for the 256KB run?
alice: appended log snippet:
```
NCCL INFO : Using ring
NCCL INFO : channel count 4
NCCL INFO : chunk size 262144
NCCL INFO : opportunistic fusion disabled
NCCL INFO : using algorithm RING for size 262144
NCCL TIME : allreduce chunk latency 1.12ms
```
ben: chunk size 262144 == 256KB. if the runtime sets chunk size to exactly that, NCCL may be hitting a single-channel path or triggering a non-pipelined transfer. try setting `NCCL_BUFFSIZE=131072` to force smaller internal chunks.
devon: also try `NCCL_PROTO=LL` vs `NCCL_PROTO=LL128` vs `NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE` — these change transport & pipelining. LL128 often helps for mid-size messages if supported by NIC/hw.
carla: another angle — kernel scheduling. if our kernel selection leaves a tiny gap between compute kernels such that NCCL can't start DMA early, comm waits. check our stream usage: are we using the same compute stream as NCCL or separate streams with proper events? runtime currently uses per-tensor default stream and launches NCCL on a dedicated comm stream, but we create events only on compute completion; maybe we signal too late.
alice: runtime code snippet (simplified):
```
cudaEventRecord(ev, compute_stream);
cudaStreamWaitEvent(comm_stream, ev, 0);
ncclAllReduce(..., comm_stream);
```
we create event after kernel launches, not after kernel completes (oops). should be `cudaEventRecord(ev, compute_stream); cudaEventSynchronize(ev)`? no — we need record then wait, which is what we do. but if record is issued before kernel is enqueued due to stream semantics, the event records before finish. need to set record after enqueue; we do record after enqueue. maybe we forgot to pass `cudaStreamAddCallback` in some paths.
ben: the event pattern looks correct normally. but if we enqueue small compute kernels repeatedly, the event may not reflect actual completion if kernels are asynchronous but depend on some other stream; worth instrumenting with `cudaEventQuery` in a repro to see when the event flips.
devon: i'm leaning towards three concurrent causes: (1) NCCL algorithm boundary at 256KB, (2) runtime coalescing creating chunk alignment hitting single-channel pipeline, (3) subtle event ordering preventing early DMA start. can we triage by forcing NCCL proto and buffsize first (cheap), then tweak runtime coalescing off (more invasive), then add event-query instrumentation.
alice: i'm going to run quick experiments this afternoon: set `NCCL_BUFFSIZE=131072`, `NCCL_PROTO=LL128`, and disable runtime coalescing flag `--kv-coalesce=false`. i'll post results.
carla: add also `--force-comm-stream-sync` sanity flag that inserts an explicit `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` after compute for a single run — if that reduces latency (it likely won't), shows compute finish race.
perf-bot: experiment matrix queued: job ids [1825123456-2, 1825123456-3, 1825123456-4]. results will be attached.
alice: initial cheap tests done: 
- NCCL_BUFFSIZE=131072 -> 256KB measured 0.58ms (good)
- NCCL_PROTO=LL128 -> 256KB measured 0.49ms (good)
- kv-coalesce=false (no runtime coalesce) -> 256KB 0.51ms
so seems like NCCL internal chunking/proto is main culprit; runtime coalescing exacerbates it but isn't root cause.
ben: nice. that suggests we should set runtime default to prefer smaller chunk sizes or set environment to prefer LL128 on our clusters. but cautious: LL128 has different perf at other sizes. recommend runtime detect NIC hw + NCCL version and pick default proto/buffsize heuristics.
carla: agree. make a heuristics patch: when NCCL_VERSION >= 2.14 and GPU arch >= sm80 and msgsize in [200KB..300KB] prefer LL128 and set buffsize=128KB. also expose override flags for Dedicated customers.
devon: i'll open a small RFC PR with test results and microbench graphs. assign to alice for verification on customer clusters.
alice: thanks — will run a few more long-running throughput tests overnight and post artifacts. :coffee:
ben: awesome. next steps: PR RFC, runtime flags, perf dashboard update to show per-msgsize proto impact. can someone add an eval test to catch regressions at the 200-300KB band?
carla: i'll add a regression test to perf harness that sweeps proto/buffsize and records median latencies.
alice: added note — might also affect KV cache refill bursts where many small entries are fused, creating these mid-size blobs. we'll correlate KV write patterns with observed allreduce spikes.
